User is planning to make chicken fajitas for dinner tonight and prefers simple, practical recipes with helpful cooking tips. The suggested recipe included chicken strips marinated in lime juice, olive oil, garlic, oregano, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper, cooked with onions and bell peppers, then served in warmed tortillas with optional toppings such as avocado, sour cream, salsa, cheese, cilantro, and lime. User plans to add onions and bell peppers to their grocery list and is running low on olive oil. They may also buy fresh cilantro and parsley. For keeping herbs fresh, useful tips include storing them in the refrigerator, loosely covering them, or placing stems in water like flowers, replacing the water regularly; cilantro and parsley can also be chopped and frozen. The previous response’s advice to tightly wrap herbs may promote moisture, so if discussing storage again, emphasize airflow, a clean container or towel, and dry leaves.

User recently downloaded a grocery list app and enjoys using it to organize shopping needs. Their mom is now using the same app too, so they can share lists and track what they need. The app’s name was not specified. Do not imply personal app use or firsthand experiences.

User enjoys trying new recipes, especially with Trader Joe’s cauliflower gnocchi. They are excited to try it with brown butter sage sauce: boil the gnocchi in salted water, reserve pasta water, brown butter carefully until nutty and golden, add sage until fragrant/crispy, toss with the gnocchi, and loosen with pasta water as needed. They may also appreciate optional Parmesan, garlic/shallots, or ricotta/goat cheese, but should watch the butter to avoid burning it. They were previously planning a dinner-party menu that included lemon garlic chicken breasts, roasted vegetables, crispy sweet potatoes, and cauliflower gnocchi with brown butter sage sauce.

For sweet potatoes, if asked again, choose true sweet potatoes rather than Russet/Idaho potatoes, cut uniformly, dry thoroughly, use high-smoke-point oil, season generously, roast at 425°F/220°C without overcrowding, and turn midway for crisp exteriors and fluffy interiors.
